key_insight: A GaOx hole transport layer can be made conductive by ion exchange during CuInSe2 co-evaporation, enabling efficient low-bandgap bottom cells without relying on extra Cu or Na.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for high-voltage 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells in tandem photovoltaics, helping reach certified performance above 16% with VOC over 550 mV.
method: Formed GaOx as the hole transport layer during absorber co-evaporation via ion exchange.
Tested the roles of Cu addition, Na, and oxygen flow in making GaOx conductive.
Examined structural state of the oxide and device performance after optimization.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: Conductive GaOx appears condition-dependent and partly crystalline, so process control during oxide formation is critical for reproducibility and transfer to other contact stacks.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
